title: "Would You Like Any Further Revisions?"... An Unexpected Phrase Appears in a Chinese Novel
source_used: The Asia Business Daily (relaying China's Dashang Newspaper)
key_facts: A reader posted on social media that the print edition of a Chinese novel contains the sentence "Would you like me to subtly revise the overall style to convey a tense, mysterious atmosphere?", believed to be an AI prompt.
Per China's Dashang Newspaper on 12 Oct, the sentence is not in the web (e-book) version and appears only between paragraphs in the print edition.
The book was published by a publishing house in Jiangsu Province; pre-orders began on 21 Aug, limited to one copy per person.
The publisher says it mistakenly treated a prompt provided by proofreading software as part of the main text, says the author is not at fault, and apologised.
The publisher will recall and dispose of copies already shipped, then revise and republish the book; buyers are reportedly offered returns and refunds.
The Asia Business Daily adds context: the Prix Goncourt removed a novel from its shortlist over AI allegations the author denies, and a Korean e-book app ended its service after using AI translation.
quote_evidence: Controversy is growing after a sentence believed to be an artificial intelligence (AI) prompt was printed verbatim in the text of a Chinese novel and published.
The sentence does not appear in the web novel (e-book) version and is included only between paragraphs in the print edition.
Buyers are reportedly being offered returns and refunds.
why_it_matters_hint: A printed book shipped with an apparent leftover AI prompt, and buyers are being offered refunds.
event_date: Dashang Newspaper report dated 12 Oct 2026; pre-orders opened 21 Aug (year not stated)
